name: Mnemoveil
description: Mnemoveil is an anamnetic compound that binds to hippocampal consolidation sites and, in conjunction with BCI memory indexing, allows users to re-experience stored memories with full sensory fidelity — not as recollection but as re-living. The memory plays back through the brain's own sensory systems with complete immersive authenticity, indistinguishable from present experience except for a faint golden warmth at the edges that users describe as 'knowing it's perfect.' Lazarus positions it as a therapeutic tool for grief processing and PTSD treatment.
effects: Emotional reliving of chosen memories with enhanced positive resonance
Profound sense of comfort and continuity
Feeling that the best moments of life are permanently accessible
side_effects: Severe present-reality dissatisfaction after repeated use
Difficulty forming new positive memories — nothing competes with perfect recall of old ones
Memory contamination — replayed memories gradually drift from actual events
Extreme: users who replay a single memory obsessively until it overwrites present identity
duration: Duration of chosen memory (compressed or extended) — subjectively 20 minutes to 4 hours
cultural_context: Mnemoveil is GLMZ's quietest catastrophe. It entered the market as a legitimate grief therapy and PTSD treatment — and it works, genuinely, for those applications. But the recreational use that followed has created a class of users called 'Archivers' who live increasingly inside their own pasts. In Tier 3 and 4, Archiver communities exist — people who share doses, curate their replay libraries, and slowly stop engaging with the present. On the Shelf, a cut version called Yesterday circulates; it can't interface with BCI memory indexing precisely, so it replays memories with distortions — users sometimes prefer the distorted version, which has become more beautiful than the original.
story_hooks: A grieving parent has been on Mnemoveil for eight months, replaying the same three months of their child's life — they've stopped eating regularly and their employer has flagged their performance decline, but they won't stop because inside the memory, their child is still alive

Memory contamination from extended Mnemoveil use means a witness to a crime can no longer reliably distinguish what they actually saw from their replayed, drifted version — a defense attorney wants to exploit this, and a prosecutor wants to suppress it
Someone is selling custom Mnemoveil doses pre-loaded with other people's memories — beautiful, curated lives for rent — and no one is sure if the source memories are donated, purchased, or stolen
